key_insight: HySTAR stabilizes credit assignment in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning by anchoring hypergraph structure, so the mapping from agents and coalitions to value targets stays consistent over time. This reduces the "structural target drift" caused by changing interaction topologies or active-agent sets.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of assigning team-level rewards to individual agents and higher-order coalitions in partially observable cooperative MARL, especially when critic structures change dynamically and make training targets inconsistent.
method: Uses anchored hypergraphs to represent agent interactions and coalition structure in a stable, fixed-reference way.
Replaces dynamically changing grouping topologies with a consistent value decomposition framework for credit assignment.
Improves critic stability by preventing target drift as agent participation or interaction patterns evolve.
impact: For practitioners, HySTAR offers a more reliable way to train cooperative multi-agent systems with shared rewards, improving learning stability and interpretability. This is especially useful in environments where agent groups, interactions, or visibility change during training.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram showing unstable dynamic hypergraph critics vs. anchored hypergraph critic

paper_title: HySTAR: Anchored Hypergraphs for Stable Credit Assignment in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Xinglong Luo, Yuding Zhang, Yuheng Kuang, Shuxuan Yuan, Zhenni Zeng
